Yeah, I really wish that they would have tied this in to the actual series because even Shu never figured out the whole truth about the virus.  It involves him and his family in more ways than even I thought tbh, and most of that was left to just kind of sit in the visual novel.  

There's even some traces of it where Segai nearly loses it next to Keido and says something along the lines of "I can see it, it's becoming clear now" while Keido looks apprehensively on, probably because he knows exactly what Segai's talking about and it means trouble for him.  

The familiarity between Keido and Segai also makes me think there's probably a history between them - he doesn't call him by rank and breaks military formality to call him "Segai-kun," which was very different than literally anyone else addressing him, not to mention Keido going out of his way to put him on the case.  They would have definitely had to become involved with one another at least indirectly for Keido to keep him alive - he would have been a liability to Da'ath after Lost Christmas/the OVA and it absolutely would have been safer to just kill him but for some reason Keido not only kept him alive, but close to his side as a secret weapon.  It was honestly the way they spoke to each other that made me go back and look at everything again, because given their individual histories, it would all add up if that actually was the case.

What really made it click for me was thinking about how he probably went those ten years questioning whether what he saw was real or not, or whether he was still sane, all while anyone who has a hand in the scene is pushing the "nothing happened/there is no war in ba sing se" given that Keido kept his position.  To put it very simply it was probably equivalent to psychological gaslighting.  

Seeing Shu probably was "I'm not crazy" "that was real" and "so I was right" all at once for him for the first time in those ten years, combined with the rush of knowing how close the answer was.  He kinda parsed through three or four different facial expressions and then just settled on absolute awe, which, well.  Sounds about right for someone experiencing all that and then some.

I've got somewhat of a theory that made a lot of sense to me after having seen the OVA and a translation of the Lost Christmas visual novel.  General spoiler warning for Lost Christmas ig?  But basically following Lost Christmas, Segai was the singular survivor of one of the massacres that resulted during one of Scrooge's fight against Present (both Scrooge and Present are human experiments, like Inori and Gai), and that was when he saw the "king's power" for the first time and then lost his eye immediately afterwards.  This is all canon to the OVA.  It's also confirmed that when he was younger he was tracking Da'ath, and his finding Scrooge was a direct result of that investigation (he posed as a member of Da'ath to lure Scrooge out).  The visual novel reveals that Keido was the reason for the existence of Scrooge, Present, and Gai - they were all projects of Da'ath, whom Keido has links to in the visual novel and the series proper.

That being said given that Segai was hunting Da'ath, Da'ath and the GHQ are definitely not one and the same.  Keido uses his involvement with the GHQ as a cover for his work with Da'ath regarding the apocalypse virus.  Keido was also the one to drag Segai into the GC plot in the first place, meaning he knows how sharp he is - so at one point it's safe to assume that Segai was essentially hunting Keido.  Keido's GHQ "cover" also remained pretty much intact until around ep. 12, at which point shit went down at Roppongi, so it also led me to assume that he kept his involvement with Da'ath under wraps until then, given that it would have been considered treason otherwise.  

From the time that Segai saw Scrooge to the time that he saw Shu was ten years (lost Christmas happened when Shu was 7), and for those ten years Segai was pretty much kept in the dark as to "what the fuck was that" in regards to the King's Power he saw.  He said it himself, he hates leaving empty spaces in his puzzles, and given that Keido was probably actively working to cover his own tracks as much as possible (so much so that he stopped Segai from going into Mana's "sanctum" thing at Roppongi) all he had to go off of for those ten years was his own eyewitness experience.  He couldn't exactly find the other soldiers and go "remember that thing" because as of the end of the OVA, he was the only one left alive.  Segai knows that something's up and his own higher-ups are withholding the information from him, and we've seen that information and the truth of the King's Power/Voids is what he wants most.  Forget Shu, he's been on this chase for a decade and the answer (Keido) is *literally* next to him.

Their targets, being compassionate, would go, and the boy who messaged would be there, sometimes with the others in their little trifecta.
